stakeholders.name: Missing child
stakeholders.description: The child who is reported missing and whose likeness the system searches for in dashcam footage.
stakeholders.why_they_care: The system's ability to locate them quickly affects their safety and well-being; incorrect matches or privacy breaches can cause harm.

stakeholders.name: Parent or legal guardian
stakeholders.description: Individual(s) who report the child missing, provide reference images, and coordinate with authorities/non-profits.
stakeholders.why_they_care: They depend on accurate, timely search results to find the child, and care about privacy, consent, and potential misuse of images.

stakeholders.name: Dashcam owner / vehicle owner
stakeholders.description: Person who owns and operates the dashcam-equipped vehicle and controls device settings and data-sharing permissions.
stakeholders.why_they_care: They manage privacy settings, data usage, battery/storage impact, potential liabilities from sharing footage, and expect benefit from participation (or protection from unwarranted intrusions).

stakeholders.name: Vehicle occupants and passengers
stakeholders.description: People who ride in vehicles equipped with the dashcam and may be recorded in footage.
stakeholders.why_they_care: They are affected by being recorded and by how their images are stored, processed, and shared; they have privacy and consent concerns.

stakeholders.name: Law enforcement agencies / police investigators
stakeholders.description: Authorities coordinating missing-person searches, receiving potential leads, and acting on matches found by the system.
stakeholders.why_they_care: They rely on timely, reliable evidence to find missing children, but must ensure legal compliance, chain-of-custody, and validate model outputs before investigative action.

stakeholders.name: Non-profit child-safety organization
stakeholders.description: Partner organization that coordinates searches, aggregates reports, and routes alerts between families, dashcam operators, and authorities.
stakeholders.why_they_care: They are responsible for coordinating effective searches, protecting families' privacy, ensuring ethical use of the system, and maintaining public trust.

stakeholders.name: Dashcam manufacturer
stakeholders.description: Company that designs, produces, and updates the dashcam hardware and firmware.
stakeholders.why_they_care: They must ensure device reliability, implement secure data storage and transmission, support model deployment/customization, manage warranties/liabilities, and address user concerns about battery/processing limits.

stakeholders.name: ML model vendor / external contractor
stakeholders.description: Third-party supplier of the person-recognition model, responsible for development, updates, and possibly tuning for deployment.
stakeholders.why_they_care: Model performance, bias, privacy-preserving design, and contractual obligations affect reputation, liability, and the effectiveness of searches; they may also need to support edge/cloud deployment constraints.

stakeholders.name: System integrators / software developers
stakeholders.description: Engineers and teams integrating the ML model with dashcam firmware, mobile apps, cloud services, and coordination systems.
stakeholders.why_they_care: They must ensure secure, efficient implementation across heterogeneous devices, manage trade-offs (edge vs. cloud), and address user-facing concerns like data usage and latency.

stakeholders.name: Cloud service providers / data center operators
stakeholders.description: Third-party platforms that may host model inference, storage, and coordination services if cloud processing is used.
stakeholders.why_they_care: They provide scalability and availability; their security, uptime, and data-handling practices directly affect system reliability, costs, and privacy compliance.

stakeholders.name: Mobile carriers and hotspot providers
stakeholders.description: Cellular and Wi‑Fi providers through which dashcams or companion phones may upload/download footage and metadata.
stakeholders.why_they_care: Network usage affects bandwidth costs, latency, and feasibility of real-time searches; providers may face policy or privacy inquiries related to transported data.

stakeholders.name: Members of the public / bystanders captured in footage
stakeholders.description: People who are incidentally recorded by dashcams while in public spaces.
stakeholders.why_they_care: Unintended recording and potential retention/processing of their images raise privacy concerns, potential misidentification, and reputational risk.

stakeholders.name: Privacy and data-protection regulators
stakeholders.description: Government agencies and regulators setting legal requirements for personal data collection, processing, retention, and sharing.
stakeholders.why_they_care: They must ensure the system complies with laws (e.g., data minimization, consent, cross-border transfers) and protect citizens' rights; noncompliance can lead to enforcement actions.

stakeholders.name: Legal professionals and courts
stakeholders.description: Attorneys and courts that may need to evaluate evidence produced by the system or adjudicate disputes arising from its use.
stakeholders.why_they_care: They rely on understanding the system's accuracy, chain of custody, and potential biases when considering admissibility of evidence or liability claims.

stakeholders.name: Insurance companies
stakeholders.description: Insurers providing coverage for vehicles, dashcams, manufacturers, or organizations using the system.
stakeholders.why_they_care: Claims related to misuse, privacy breaches, false leads, or device failures affect underwriting, premiums, and potential payouts.

stakeholders.name: Device repair technicians and support staff
stakeholders.description: Technicians and customer support teams who service dashcams, handle firmware updates, and troubleshoot device issues.
stakeholders.why_they_care: They need access to diagnostics and secure procedures for updates and repairs; improper handling can introduce vulnerabilities or data exposure.

stakeholders.name: Malicious actors (abusers, stalkers, hackers)
stakeholders.description: Individuals or groups who might attempt to exploit the system to track people, obtain sensitive footage, or disrupt searches.
stakeholders.why_they_care: They may seek to weaponize system capabilities or vulnerabilities; the presence of such actors creates security and safety risks for other stakeholders.
